Train a Sliced Wasserstein Autoencoder (SWAE)

Source: R/MMD_Vae.R
trainSWAEModel.Rd

Trains an autoencoder with Sliced Wasserstein Distance regularization. SWAE uses optimal transport geometry to match the latent distribution to the prior, offering computational advantages over MMD-based approaches (O(n log n) vs O(n^2)).

Usage

trainSWAEModel(
  trainData,
  useMarkers,
  epochs = 80,
  latentDim = NULL,
  seed = 1994,
  lambda = 10,
  numProjections = 50L,
  valData,
  originalDim = 27L,
  batchSize = 32,
  hiddenSizes = NULL
)

Arguments

trainData

Data frame of training data.

useMarkers

Character vector; names of marker columns to use.

epochs

Integer; number of training epochs, default is 80.

latentDim

Integer; dimensionality of latent space, optional.

seed

Integer; random seed for reproducibility, default is 1994.

lambda

Numeric; regularization weight for Sliced Wasserstein loss, default is 10.0.

numProjections

Integer; number of random projections for SW distance, default is 50L.

valData

Data frame of validation data.

originalDim

Integer; dimensionality of input, default is 27.

batchSize

Integer; batch size for training, default is 32.

hiddenSizes

Numeric vector; sizes of hidden layers in encoder/decoder.

Value

List containing the trained SWAE model, encoder, and decoder.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Requires TensorFlow and keras3 to be installed
data(sample_cytof_data)
data(sample_markers)

ref_samples <- computeReferenceSample(
  data = sample_cytof_data,
  markers = sample_markers,
  sampleCol = "sample_id",
  N = 2
)

train_data <- sample_cytof_data[
  sample_cytof_data$sample_id %in% ref_samples$topNSamples,
  sample_markers
]
val_data <- sample_cytof_data[
  sample_cytof_data$sample_id %in% ref_samples$bottomNSamples,
  sample_markers
]

swae_model <- trainSWAEModel(
  trainData = train_data,
  useMarkers = sample_markers,
  epochs = 30,
  latentDim = 8,
  lambda = 10.0,
  numProjections = 50,
  valData = val_data,
  batchSize = 32,
  seed = 1994
)

# Use with decodeSamples (same as WAE-MMD)
normalized <- decodeSamples(newSamples = as.matrix(new_data), vae = swae_model)
} # }
